page: OVHcloud l4-90 is a GPU-accelerated virtual instance designed to support machine learning inference, graphics processing, and compute-intensive enterprise tasks. The host configuration is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9454 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz, providing 22 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. The hardware platform includes 90 GB of system memory, averaging approximately 4.09 GB per core, along with 400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Dedicated CPU core assignment and support for AVX-512 vector instructions provide reliable, low-jitter processing for parallel tasks.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU featuring 24 GB of VRAM. In synthetic machine learning benchmarks, the system demonstrates top-tier LLM inference performance, exceeding 12,300 prompt tokens per second and 511 text generation tokens per second on 135M parameter models. On medium-sized 7B parameter language models, it maintains over 2,286 prompt tokens per second and 54 tokens per second during generation. Larger 70B parameter models show capable prompt processing throughput, though memory limitations require careful consideration when running large-scale model architectures.

Host CPU and memory benchmarks reflect strong performance across compute and decompressed data workloads, with high rankings in single-core execution and multi-threaded decompression tests. The 400 GB NVMe local drive ensures low latency for operational scratch space, model weights, and local caching. Architectural tradeoffs include the omission of complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring deliberate network planning. Given its single-GPU density and dedicated host resources, the l4-90 offers cost-efficient utilization for real-time model serving, video transcoding, computer vision pipelines, and general GPU-accelerated computing.
description: OVHcloud l4-90 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured for AI inference and compute-heavy pipelines. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9454 processor, the system allocates 22 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.75 GHz with support for AVX-512 vector instructions. It features 90 GB of system memory, alongside a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. Benchmark performance highlights strong single-core CPU execution and top-tier small- to medium-model LLM inference throughput, achieving over 12,000 prompt tokens per second on lightweight language models and over 2,200 tokens per second on 7B models. Balancing GPU compute with substantial system memory and dedicated host cores, the server offers efficient hardware density for AI model deployment, video transcoding, image processing, and distributed machine learning inference.
